title: Local AI Assistant
hook: A privacy-first desktop AI interface running quantized open-source models completely offline.
problem: Cloud-based LLMs require constant internet connectivity, transmit sensitive private user prompts to external vendor servers, and incur continuous API token costs.
idea: An offline desktop application wrapping quantized open-source models (LLaMA 3.1 8B, Mistral 7B) through Ollama with low-latency streaming responses and localized vector storage.
whyIBuiltIt: I wanted an intelligent AI coding assistant that operates reliably during travel or network outages without sending proprietary code snippets over public web networks.
research: Benchmarked GGUF quantization levels (Q4_K_M vs Q5_K_M vs Q8_0) on host CPU RAM, evaluating token generation speed against perplexity degradation.
architecture: React 18 frontend communicates via Server-Sent Events (SSE) with a local FastAPI proxy layer that streams token outputs directly from the Ollama C++ inference backend.
databaseDesign: SQLite local database storing encrypted user conversation histories, parameter configs, and custom system prompts with indexed session keys.
apiDesign: POST /api/chat (SSE Streamed tokens), GET /api/models (List active local models), POST /api/embeddings (Generate local vector embeddings).
folderStructure:
local-ai-assistant/
├── backend/
│   ├── app/main.py (FastAPI SSE router)
│   ├── app/ollama.py (Local process IPC client)
│   └── app/database.py (SQLite Session store)
├── frontend/
│   ├── src/components/ChatStream.tsx
│   └── src/hooks/useSSE.ts
└── README.md
implementation: Built using FastAPI for asynchronous stream orchestration, React 18 for smooth UI updates, and TailwindCSS for a minimal dark dashboard interface.
challenges: Handling initial model loading latency into system RAM without freezing the UI thread, and managing smooth incremental token buffer rendering in the browser.
tradeoffs: Chose 4-bit quantization (Q4_K_M) over full precision FP16 to achieve ~8.5 tokens/sec generation on 16GB host RAM, accepting slight precision drops for usable speed.
lessons: Local AI models on consumer hardware are practical when memory bandwidth and streaming buffer boundaries are carefully managed.
lessonsLearned: Memory bandwidth is the primary bottleneck for CPU-bound LLM inference, not compute capacity. Streamed token buffers prevent perception of latency.
futureImprovements: Implement local Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using SQLite VSS to index local project documentation.
futurePlans: Implement localized vector search over personal PDF documentation.

title: ETLab+
hook: A multi-tenant college laboratory management platform with role-based access control and database isolation.
problem: Manual lab attendance logging and equipment reservation across engineering departments caused scheduling conflicts, lost records, and unauthenticated access.
idea: A centralized web platform automating lab attendance, equipment checkout tracking, and real-time faculty authorization dashboards.
whyIBuiltIt: Built to eliminate paper-based lab sign-in sheets at Sahrdaya College of Engineering and give department heads real-time lab utilization analytics.
research: Analyzed relational database normalization vs JSONB flexibility for multi-department permission rules, settling on PostgreSQL Row-Level Security.
architecture: Next.js frontend communicating with a Node.js REST API layer backed by PostgreSQL relational schemas and row-level tenant security policy.
databaseDesign: PostgreSQL database containing normalized tables for students, faculty, labs, schedules, and reservations linked via Foreign Key constraints.
apiDesign: POST /api/auth/login (JWT token), GET /api/labs/attendance (Real-time logs), POST /api/reservations (Equipment checkouts).
folderStructure:
etlab-plus/
├── server/
│   ├── src/routes/attendance.ts
│   ├── src/db/schema.sql (PostgreSQL RLS policies)
│   └── src/middleware/auth.ts
├── client/
│   └── app/dashboard/page.tsx
└── README.md
implementation: Architected normalized PostgreSQL schema with Row-Level Security, JWT authentication, and interactive attendance dashboards.
challenges: Preventing concurrent equipment double-booking during peak lab registration hours while maintaining instant query responses.
tradeoffs: Enforced strict PostgreSQL Row-Level Security at the database level rather than application middleware alone, ensuring zero data leak across departments.
lessons: Enforcing relational constraints at the database engine level prevents application-tier race conditions.
lessonsLearned: Database constraints and indexes are the most reliable defense against concurrency bugs in web platforms.
futureImprovements: Add RFID / QR code scanner integration for contactless physical lab entry.
futurePlans: Integrate physical RFID badge scanners for instant laboratory access.

title: RyMeds
hook: A high-reliability pharmacy management software streamlining inventory control, billing, and prescription tracking.
problem: Small community pharmacies struggle with manual stock expiry tracking, slow paper billing counters, and medicine misplacement.
idea: An intuitive pharmacy management desktop software providing automated stock low-level alerts, barcode billing, and expiry warnings.
whyIBuiltIt: My first major software project designed to digitize local medical store billing workflows with zero training requirement.
research: Investigated transaction isolation levels to prevent inventory race conditions during rapid counter checkout.
architecture: Modular monolithic application communicating directly with an embedded SQLite transactional database for high offline reliability.
databaseDesign: SQLite relational tables: medicines (id, name, batch_no, expiry_date, stock_qty), sales (invoice_id, timestamp, total), sale_items.
apiDesign: Internal IPC billing methods: processInvoice(items), updateStock(medicineId, qty), generateMonthlyReport().
folderStructure:
rymeds/
├── src/
│   ├── controllers/InventoryController.py
│   ├── views/BillingWindow.py
│   └── database/schema.sql
└── rymeds.py
implementation: Built core inventory algorithms, automated invoice PDF generators, and rapid medicine search filters.
challenges: Calculating accurate expiry warnings while keeping billing speed fast during high customer traffic.
tradeoffs: Chose an embedded local database (SQLite) instead of a cloud database so counter billing continues uninterrupted even during internet outages.
lessons: Software utility is measured by how effectively it solves immediate daily operations for non-technical users.
lessonsLearned: Data integrity and simple UI layouts build trust with daily operational users faster than complex decorative features.
futureImprovements: Add GST tax auto-calculation and supplier purchase order generation.

title: AI Study Coach
hook: An intelligent study assistant transforming raw lecture notes into active recall flashcards and quiz evaluations.
problem: Students spend hours manually creating revision flashcards and practice quizzes from long course notes instead of actively learning.
idea: An automated system that parses Markdown and PDF notes, extracts key concepts via LLMs, and generates spaced-repetition quizzes.
whyIBuiltIt: Created to streamline my own CS exam preparation across operating systems, database management, and computer networks.
research: Evaluated prompt engineering templates for structured JSON output extraction from local open-source LLMs.
architecture: Client-side web app submitting document text to a Python backend, which prompts an Ollama instance to output structured quiz schema JSON.
databaseDesign: Local storage index storing flashcard decks, SRS review intervals, and historical quiz scores.
apiDesign: POST /api/generate-quiz (Parse raw text -> return Quiz JSON), POST /api/evaluate-answer (Semantic evaluation).
folderStructure:
ai-study-coach/
├── backend/
│   ├── app/parser.py
│   └── app/prompt_templates.py
├── frontend/
│   └── src/components/QuizCard.tsx
└── README.md
implementation: Integrated local LLM prompt templates returning strict JSON arrays, paired with an interactive quiz interface.
challenges: Enforcing deterministic JSON schema outputs from open-source LLMs without hallucinated keys.
tradeoffs: Used structured JSON schema parsing retries to handle raw LLM formatting variations cleanly.
lessons: Constraining LLM outputs with strict JSON validators turns probabilistic models into reliable data pipelines.
lessonsLearned: Prompt validation and JSON schema enforcement are essential when relying on local open-source language models.
futureImprovements: Implement SuperMemo-2 (SM-2) spaced repetition algorithm for optimal card review scheduling.
futurePlans: Add SM-2 algorithmic scheduling for long-term retention.

title: Robotics Telemetry Processor
hook: Embedded C++ sensor data pipeline filtering noisy MPU-6050 accelerometer and gyroscope signals for robot navigation.
problem: Raw IMU sensor readings suffer from high-frequency vibration noise and low-frequency gyroscopic drift, making raw telemetry un-usable for robot positioning.
idea: An embedded C++ sensor processing module implementing complementary filtering to combine accelerometer stability with gyroscope responsiveness.
whyIBuiltIt: Developed during my Robotics Internship at IEEE Sensors Council & Luminar Technolab to stabilize mobile robot tilt calculations.
research: Studied Kalman filtering vs Complementary filtering latency tradeoffs on 8-bit Arduino AVR microcontrollers.
architecture: Hardware IMU sensor sampled via I2C bus at 100Hz -> C++ Complementary Filter -> Serial Stream -> MATLAB / Python Real-time Plotter.
databaseDesign: Circular memory buffer on microcontroller holding 200 telemetry frames for real-time moving average calculation.
apiDesign: C++ Library methods: SensorPipeline::init(), SensorPipeline::update(float dt), SensorPipeline::getOrientation().
folderStructure:
robotics-telemetry/
├── src/
│   ├── ComplementaryFilter.cpp
│   ├── IMUDriver.cpp
│   └── main.cpp
├── python_plotter/telemetry_plot.py
└── README.md
implementation: Wrote low-level I2C communication routines in C++, implemented complementary filter math, and output real-time orientation estimates.
challenges: Eliminating cumulative gyroscopic drift over long operating intervals without incurring heavy floating-point calculation delay on 16MHz CPUs.
tradeoffs: Selected a mathematical complementary filter over a full EKF (Extended Kalman Filter) to execute within a tight 10ms sampling deadline.
lessons: Understanding physical hardware limits is as critical as writing efficient code when programming embedded systems.
lessonsLearned: Filtering noise at the sensor intake layer prevents exponential error accumulation in downstream navigation algorithms.
futureImprovements: Port to ROS2 (Robot Operating System) node architecture on Raspberry Pi.
futurePlans: Migrate logic into a native ROS2 package.
